epic.name: Workflow monitor and API reference
unverifiedAssumptions: Verify the run list order: the app assumes the data service returns process instances newest first. If it returns them in another order, the Workflow monitor will not open with the latest runs at the top. Column sorting only reorders the page you are on.

Verify Pending steps appear: the app assumes the service returns every step of a run, including ones that have not run yet, marked Pending. If it only returns steps that actually ran, a failed run will show fewer tiles and no Pending steps after the failure.

Workflow monitor sorting only reorders the page currently on screen: the service pages the list itself and has no sort option, so with more than one page of runs a column sort will not pull rows in from other pages.

The API page example request shows the data service address the app proxies to (by default http://localhost:10020/curve-data). Confirm this is the address actuarial-model consumers should see, or whether a different public address should be shown.

Verify Open workflow opens the file's own import run: the app assumes a file's WOID is the ID of its ImportFile workflow run (confirmed on the live service), so Open workflow works for every file, and that the later LoadYieldCurves run has no link back to a file.

Verify the 'current' label: the live service now marks every file as current, including Failed ones, so the file details subtitle says '· current' on failed files. If 'current' should still mean the latest successful import for its family, the service needs to change or the app should stop showing the label.

Verify that Importing files really are still in progress: many files show Importing because their RateLoad run is paused at its Complete step. If those runs never resume, the files stay at Importing for good, with no 'Import complete.' notice.

Verify the failed step wording for files that failed while staging: the service reports internal step names such as 'HoldImportDetailsLog' for ImportPro failures, and the alert and details show that name as-is.
When every Files received count on the Overview is zero, the card shows the total ("0") with no breakdown line. Confirm that is right.
The file details still label the RateLoad run ID row "Workflow instance". Check whether that label is clear enough next to the new "Open import run" button, or name the label you want.
The Import trace page (File log) still shows a failed RateLoad run as a green "Finished"; only the Workflow monitor shows "Finished (Error)" for now. Confirm whether the trace should match.

Picking a different run from the list after opening one from a file drops the carried file, so "Open file log entry" looks the new run up itself instead of returning to the original file. Confirm that is the behaviour you want.
"Finished (Error)" reads at most 2,000 Finished runs (40 pages of 50) from the service and filters them in the browser; older failed runs beyond that would not be listed.
